key_insight: Machine learning-assisted serum Raman spectroscopy showed moderate discrimination between prostate cancer cases and symptomatic controls, including in the PSA grey zone.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic—not drug discovery—approach could potentially support risk stratification before MRI or biopsy, pending prospective validation.
method: Analysed archived samples using dried-serum Raman spectroscopy.
Used supervised machine learning to estimate prostate cancer probabilities.
Evaluated discrimination overall and in the PSA 4–10 ng/mL subgroup.
evidence_signal: In this retrospective proof-of-concept study, AUC was approximately 0.77 among 119 cancer cases and 60 controls, and approximately 0.78 in the PSA grey-zone subgroup of 54 cases and 41 controls.
watch_item: Prospective validation in contemporary diagnostic pathways is needed before clinical use or claims of reduced unnecessary investigations.
paper_title: Machine learning-assisted serum Raman spectroscopy for risk stratification in men with suspected prostate cancer: a retrospective proof-of-concept study
